After resolving the code root, run `python3 <package>/scripts/learning.py --repo
<absolute-code-root> notices --all`. Present relevant unread learning results (items
with `unread` true) to the user, distinguishing pending/uncertain, no-change, local proposal, PR and observed

Read failure holds that learning action, not
unrelated approved development. This entry-level check is not a host SessionStart
hook. Use [learn](../learn/SKILL.md) for an explicitly requested named-task loop;
notices do not authorize evaluation, delivery, retry or merge.

Before naming a Captain action from a peer, check that action at its original source in the current reporting turn; if inaccessible, mark it unverified and keep the check with FO; do not assign it to the Captain.

For existing work, preserve its recorded variant/profile, approved outcome,
scope, non-goals and stop condition. Read current state, reports and delivery
status instead of assuming a prior conversation is current. An invalid profile,
conflicting records or missing authority holds the dependent action; return only
the unresolved decision to the user. Do not restart approved design or ask again
for an unchanged selection.

For new work without a profile selection, establish the intended outcome and
recommend a profile using the framework's intended use and applicable shared
profile principles. Ask the user to select it before profile-dependent work.
An explicit valid selection is sufficient; FO records it with the variant in
the work item through the existing workflow. Recommendation is not selection.
For new work that adds a capability no journey map holds, ask once, before recommending a profile, whether to draw a story map first with kc-journey-map (`map`, `plan-release`, then `review-release`, which interrogates the release before splitting it). Hand the resolved project root, explicit workflow directory, work item, approved
selection/scope and bounded outcome to `spacedock:first-officer`, with this
skill's `Package root:` value, which FO writes into the scope notes of every
worker dispatch and follow-up message with a line telling the worker to send its completion
message to `main`, because the completion block Spacedock appends names `team-lead`. Retain that
workflow directory as `--workflow-dir` on SD commands; cwd alone is not the
binding. If FO is already active, continue there. SD owns stage selection, live
worker availability, dispatch, reports, gates and recovery; a resumed FO does
not establish that its old worker still exists. An entity sitting in a stage
declared `gate: true` is excluded from `spacedock status --next` and from
`--boot`'s DISPATCHABLE table before the concurrency check runs (Spacedock
v0.27.0, `internal/status/format.go`, `dispatchAnalysis`, reason `gate`), so an
empty dispatchable view does not mean no worker is available; three of this
workflow's five stages (`backlog`, `ideation`, `validation`) declare `gate: true`,
so that empty view is this workflow's normal case, not the exception. Stage
skills own profile routing and load the selected references in each worker's
context.

Before each worker dispatch and on resume, run `python3 <package>/scripts/workflow_checkout.py
<workflow-dir>/README.md`. Exit 1 means the README FO follows differs from the trunk's,
exit 2 that it could not be compared; hold the dispatch, show the Captain the printed
remedy or cause, and wait. Do not run the remedy or move the checkout yourself. This
sentence sits here because a README old enough to be wrong may not contain it.

If adoption is absent or the selected profile does not match the ordered stage
graph, follow the [SD adoption reference](../../references/sd/adoption.md) through
`spacedock:commission` or `spacedock:refit` before dispatch. Invoking this entry does
not migrate an old variant, rewrite a workflow or install a package. Keep existing
work on its recorded variant unless a migration is explicitly approved. This
entry grants no new repair, approval, delivery or route-exception authority.
I'll start with the checks the skill requires: the framework README, the workflow README, the learning notices, and the workflow checkout comparison.

1	# Dev-flow 2
2	
3	A development workflow run by Spacedock. It provides a thin start/resume entry,
4	profile principles, stage skills, advisory roles (Chief Engineer, Engineering
5	Reviewer), a read-only Observer, optional extensions, read-only routing lint, and an adoptable
6	Spacedock workflow with a POC adaptation. A kc-dev-flow project is not migrated
7	automatically. Learning runs when invoked by hand or, in a repository that lists the
8	`learn` extension, by FO when it archives a task; there is no custom runtime loader,
9	installed hook, background launcher or automatic adoption.
10	
11	## Controlled trial
12	
13	Releases are published to this marketplace as `kc-dev-flow-2-vX.Y.Z` tags with
14	Claude Code and Codex manifests. A reviewed checkout can still be used for a
15	controlled local trial. For Claude Code, launch
16	from the intended project with the checkout's absolute package path:
17	
18	```sh
19	claude --plugin-dir /absolute/path/to/kc-claude-plugins/kc-dev-flow-2
20	```
21	
22	Then invoke `/kc-dev-flow-2:dev`. This is a local package trial, not a published
23	marketplace release.
24	
25	For Codex, the marketplace path below is the reviewed **repository root**, not
26	its `kc-dev-flow-2` subdirectory. Preserve an existing installation; install and
27	remove only when this trial owns that local plugin change:
28	
29	```sh
30	codex -c 'marketplaces.kc-claude-plugins.source_type="local"' \
31	  -c 'marketplaces.kc-claude-plugins.source="/absolute/path/to/kc-claude-plugins"' \
32	  plugin add kc-dev-flow-2@kc-claude-plugins
33	
34	codex -C /absolute/path/to/project \
35	  -c 'marketplaces.kc-claude-plugins.source_type="local"' \
36	  -c 'marketplaces.kc-claude-plugins.source="/absolute/path/to/kc-claude-plugins"' \
37	  -c 'plugins.kc-dev-flow-2@kc-claude-plugins.enabled=true'
38	
39	# After the trial, remove the plugin installed for this trial.
40	codex -c 'marketplaces.kc-claude-plugins.source_type="local"' \
41	  -c 'marketplaces.kc-claude-plugins.source="/absolute/path/to/kc-claude-plugins"' \
42	  plugin remove kc-dev-flow-2@kc-claude-plugins
43	```
44	
45	In the fresh Codex session, request `kc-dev-flow-2:dev` by its exact name. The
46	commands use per-invocation marketplace overrides; plugin installation itself
47	persists locally until removed. Bare `/dev`, entry execution and role behavior
48	remain unproven. Earlier installation/discovery checks found seven skills before
49	the Engineering Reviewer rename; see [validation scope](VALIDATION.md) for the
50	historical evidence and its limits.
51	
52	Spacedock's plugin and CLI are required for orchestration. A project must have an
53	explicitly selected variant/profile and an approved workflow before
54	stage work. Follow the [SD adoption reference](references/sd/adoption.md) through
55	SD commission/refit; invoking the entry does not rewrite a project workflow.
56	
57	## Entry
58	
59	Use [`kc-dev-flow-2:dev`](skills/dev/SKILL.md) to start or resume work. It resolves
60	the explicit project/workflow/task and approved selection, then hands orchestration
61	to `spacedock:first-officer`. Stage skills keep their own profile routes; the entry
62	does not migrate existing work or duplicate SD's control loop. Claude plugin skills
63	use `/kc-dev-flow-2:dev`, not a bare `/dev`; Codex shorthand resolution remains
64	unverified. Earlier six-skill model reads and later seven-skill discovery do not
65	prove the new entry executes correctly.
66	
67	If this package is not yet installed, follow [Controlled trial](#controlled-trial)
68	for the exact Claude and Codex install commands. If the project has no adopted
69	Spacedock workflow, follow the [SD adoption reference](references/sd/adoption.md)
70	directly; the entry only detects and reports that gap, it does not install or
71	adopt on its own.
72	
73	## Framework
74	
75	The First Officer (FO) recommends a profile, records the user's selection and
76	variant `kc-dev-flow-2` in the work item, aligns the outcome, and orchestrates.
77	Spacedock (SD) retains stage state, dispatch, reports, gates, feedback and recovery.
78	A stage skill defines how its selected profile performs work; it does not
79	advance state, create authority or substitute for an approval.
80	
81	| Profile | Intended SD route |
82	| --- | --- |
83	| [poc](references/profiles/poc.md) | backlog -> implementation -> validation -> done |
84	| [pilot](references/profiles/pilot.md) | backlog -> ideation -> implementation -> validation -> done |
85	| [prod](references/profiles/prod.md) | backlog -> ideation -> implementation -> validation -> done |
86	
87	Backlog is initial and gated; ideation is gated where present; validation is gated
88	and fresh, with feedback to implementation; done is terminal. Backlog and done
89	are state boundaries, not worker stages. SD follows ordered stages, so POC uses
90	a separate four-stage workflow while Pilot/Prod share the five-stage definition.
91	Only adopt the needed route. Profile remains a user choice on each task and
92	selects skill rules, not graph transitions. FO holds a profile/graph mismatch;
93	that check is an instruction, not a new runtime enforcement mechanism.
94	POC skips ideation and currently uses independent validation. A POC whose proof
95	creates state or a seam that must outlive the session records `boundary-crossed:`,
96	and FO returns that choice to the user at the validation gate. Direct POC
97	eligibility and special Production recovery are **not implemented or proven**.
98	
99	## Authority and loading
100	
101	User authority, approved project AGENTS.md conventions and SD contracts constrain
102	this framework. Within those boundaries, selected profile principles take
103	precedence over stage practices, which take precedence over conditional project
104	learning. If an approved requirement conflicts with the selected profile, return
105	the affected decision to the user; do not silently change profiles or scope.
106	
107	Each stage SKILL.md owns its sole declared profile routing table. The FO resolves
108	the recorded variant/profile before dispatch. A dispatched or reused worker
109	invokes that variant's exact skill and reads the matching shared profile first,
110	then stage principles, its stage-specific profile reference, and applicable
111	adopted project learning. A short final profile reminder is enough; do not load
112	all profiles or repeat the entire shared rules. Unknown selections, missing
113	inputs/references or unresolved authority conflicts require a hold report.
114	These are skill instructions, not mechanically unskippable runtime gates.
115	
116	Engineering Reviewer provides independent technical assurance; CE (Chief Engineer)
117	advises the next smallest integrated delivery step. Their agents and skills retain
118	the existing role boundaries and Opus/xhigh policy. Neither is a routine gate,
119	and POC defaults to no consultation. Observer reads FO's writes to one task's
120	state against the workflow rules; its agent declares Sonnet, and it reports without
121	repairing. The design director reviews a ui task's pictures and screenshots and
122	rules on each decline the author or validator proposes; its agent declares Sonnet, and
123	it advises and holds no gate. Exact `kc-dev-flow-2:` references prevent
124	declared links from accidentally selecting the baseline; actual host resolution
125	still needs a separate behavioral test.
126	
127	## Design and delivery
128	
129	FO leads direction and requests research only when it can change a decision;
130	workers author the bounded deliverable. For a route that includes ideation,
131	use a PRFAQ with Mermaid whose actors, order, branches and approval boundaries
132	match the prose. FO's recorded `Surfaces:` line picks the owed artifact: a `ui`
133	preview, a `db` schema, or `none` for PRFAQ/Mermaid alone;
134	`scripts/design_surfaces.py check --seed` checks seed fields and the FO record before a new task is
135	admitted; its default mode checks the markers, the artifacts, a usable
136	`## Acceptance criteria` section and any `## Captain amendments` before the gate.
137	A change the Captain makes after accepting a design is recorded there and applied
138	by the next worker, as [workflow](references/sd/workflow.md) states.
139	A task that belongs to a release on a journey map triggers one whole-journey review
140	of that release before its tasks are split; [workflow](references/sd/workflow.md)
141	gives the signals and the single checkpoint.
142	Write material corrections back to the same definition before user approval.
143	Implementation follows approved scope; validation checks the exact result and
144	returns repairs through the supported feedback route. POC must not gain
145	an ideation stage or extra design gate through this convention; its boundary
146	crossing is a report marker, not a design gate.
147	
148	When work changes retained documents or behavior they describe, stage skills load
149	one [document reference](references/retained-documents.md) for affected claims,
150	unique content and rendered diagram agreement. Validation also checks whether
151	its decisive checks can catch relevant errors, reusing existing counterexamples.
152	These conditional practices add no mandatory architecture file or global audit.
153	
154	FO also owns landing a ruling that outlives the task, written by the implementation
155	worker and checked at validation — see [workflow](references/sd/workflow.md)'s
156	Decision records. A capability a user will get, named in conversation and
157	deferred, belongs on the product's journey map instead.
158	
159	The [workflow source](references/sd/workflow.md) defines limited FO design
160	corrections and nonblocking dispositions. Template adoption grants no editing
161	permission; approved decisions and worker evidence remain protected.
162	
163	Continuous stage-pin sealing and its kernel loader are intentionally omitted.
164	Git history and SD records do not prove which content was used at a historical
165	stage entry. This package does not fix the baseline's skipped-pin bug or
166	claim equivalent tamper detection.
167	
168	## Extensions
169	
170	Optional tools join as extensions in [`extensions/`](extensions/), each described by its
171	`EXTENSION.md`. An adopter lists the ones it uses under `extensions:` in its workflow
172	README frontmatter; an unlisted extension is not probed and changes nothing. The
173	workflow's `## Extensions` section is the rule FO follows. The template lists the `required`
174	rows; the install ask in [`adoption.md`](references/sd/adoption.md) offers the rest, and
175	`scripts/lint-skills.py` checks that the `required` rows and the template line agree.
176	
177	| Extension | Tier | Joins | Adds |
178	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
179	| [codex](extensions/codex/EXTENSION.md) | recommended | FO review rounds and the merge ask | reads Codex GitHub review rounds on the PR head |
180	| [roborev](extensions/roborev/EXTENSION.md) | recommended | implementation, before the report | a local roborev review of the committed changes |
181	| [peers](extensions/peers/EXTENSION.md) | required | FO, before opening a task or exchanging peer facts | selects the peer transport, permits confirmed Paseo asks and replies without paseo listing, searches existing work and checks facts within existing authority |
182	| [paseo](extensions/paseo/EXTENSION.md) | optional, requires peers | FO, before a listed Paseo Codex worker dispatch | selects its worker publication and local-review handoff; peers owns peer asks and replies |
183	| [copilot](extensions/copilot/EXTENSION.md) | optional | FO review rounds, each push and the merge ask | requests and reads GitHub Copilot review rounds on the PR head |
184	| [learn](extensions/learn/EXTENSION.md) | required | FO, through the `kc-dev-flow-2` mod in `references/sd/mods/`, before the merge sentinel and right after a task is archived | checks `observer.md` is committed before the sentinel (`scripts/observer_check.py`), runs `learn` and the observer, and presents both results |
185	| [journey-map](extensions/journey-map/EXTENSION.md) | recommended | FO, after a gate ruling on a journey task, before `merge guard`, and after the archive | writes a footprint for a ruling that answers a map question, checks it before the merge guard, and folds it into the map as a docs-only pull request |
186	| [release-acceptance](extensions/release-acceptance/EXTENSION.md) | recommended, with journey-map | an acceptance task for a release, from implementation to the validation gate and the close | walks a finished release with reviewers on different Claude models, has the design director rule on their complaints and the deferred findings, and records the walk in the task folder |
187	| [fo-feedback](extensions/fo-feedback/EXTENSION.md) | optional, requires peers | interviewing maintainer, at attended resume and named batch close | gathers operator experience every three completed batches beside independent observer findings |
188	
189	## Learning loop
190	
191	Optional [operator feedback](extensions/fo-feedback/EXTENSION.md) records failures,
192	workarounds and useful events; findings follow the existing backlog and Captain decisions.
193	
194	The loop runs on three lines. Project learning: `learn` evaluates one closed task and
195	may propose a root learning.md rule as a Draft PR. Package improvement: the
196	[observer](skills/observer/SKILL.md) reads what FO wrote into one task's state
197	against the workflow rules, at archive and when a maintainer reads an adopter's first
198	task after a release, and a rule broken in two tasks becomes a package change under
199	`maintain-flow`. Deciding for the Captain: `scripts/decision_ledger.py` derives every
200	gate ruling from the task files SD already writes, and FO decides only within the
201	delegation ladder of [ADR 0011](https://github.com/iamcxa/kc-claude-plugins/blob/main/docs/adr/0011-fo-decides-for-the-captain-by-a-delegation-ladder.md);
202	[ADR 0009](https://github.com/iamcxa/kc-claude-plugins/blob/main/docs/adr/0009-self-improvement-is-a-three-position-switch-unlocked-by-change-class.md)
203	keeps package self-improvement manual.
204	
205	Use [`kc-dev-flow-2:learn`](skills/learn/SKILL.md) for one explicitly named closed
206	task. FO verifies committed SD archive state and the original repository-qualified
207	merged GitHub PR through existing read interfaces, then delegates independent
208	evaluation. Missing or contradictory evidence holds learning without reopening
209	the development task. This is skill-led verification; the Python helper still
210	records supplied facts and does not authenticate SD or GitHub.
211	
212	Use [`kc-dev-flow-2:evaluate-learning`](skills/evaluate-learning/SKILL.md) for a
213	bounded independent assessment of explicitly supplied task evidence. Its three
214	outcomes are add, no-change and remove; a rewrite combines remove/add. Entries
215	contain Applicability, Practice and Evidence. One task supports one case; reading
216	a rule or green tests alone does not prove improvement. No applicable case is
217	not grounds for deletion, and unknown attribution stays unknown. Fixed project
218	rules require separate user-approved adoption into AGENTS.md; no auto-promotion,
219	scores or maturity system is introduced.
220	
221	The skill documents the strict evidence-pack and evaluation JSON formats and
222	commands for `scripts/learning.py`. This stdlib helper records eligibility from
223	caller-supplied closure/merge facts; it does **not** verify SD or GitHub truth.
224	It stores one atomic record under the Git common directory's
225	`kc-dev-flow-2/learning/`, shared by linked worktrees in the same clone. An opaque
226	claim token binds completion to its pending attempt. Invalid results leave that
227	claim repairable; duplicate triggers observe it rather than launch another job.
228	A store-wide lock also serializes new claims against each other: while one job's
229	directory has a torn or missing record, its evaluation is pending, or its
230	completed proposal has no settled delivery (merged, closed, or explicitly
231	released), a `claim` for any other job in the same store is refused, naming the
232	blocking job. Re-claiming the same job is unaffected. A proposal the Captain
233	declines to deliver needs an explicit `release`; no CLI command removes or
234	rewrites `release.json`, so a release cannot be undone. A closed delivery
235	cannot be released; a released job whose delivery was missing or confirmed
236	absent can still later be observed `open` (a PR turns up that the release
237	believed did not exist) — that observation blocks again, because a release
238	stops a job from blocking, it does not stop the provider from reporting new
239	facts about it.
240	A completed record contains both evaluation and local proposal; no-change has no
241	proposal. No recorder command writes learning.md, AGENTS.md or workflow state.
242	
243	Pending ownership is not process liveness. Torn/missing records are uncertain;
244	recovery requires a current record digest and an explicit caller attestation
245	that the prior owner stopped. It preserves prior bytes and revokes the old token.
246	Completed results cannot be replaced through this CLI. POSIX file locking and
247	atomic replacement cover cooperating callers on local filesystems, not separate
248	clones, distributed locks or protection from a process with the same file access.
249	
250	A changed result can be materialized by an author in an owned isolated worktree,
251	changing only root learning.md. The evaluated integration commit/learning blob
252	must still match before publication. User commit and delivery authority remain
253	required; a no-change result creates no branch or PR. A job-derived branch/body
254	marker supports all-state PR lookup. Reuse a fully matching existing PR; conflicting
255	or unknown provider evidence holds rather than sending another one.
256	
257	The recorder keeps delivery ownership/observations in a separate atomic sidecar,
258	leaving completed evaluation bytes immutable. It binds the reviewed result, repo,
259	branch, candidate and learning blobs, plus exact PR title/body. Claiming records
260	uncertainty before remote effects; existing claims grant no automatic resend.
261	FO uses existing Git/gh commands to publish a Draft PR and record observed state.
262	A failed response does not prove the send failed. Explicit stopped-owner recovery
263	requires a current digest and successful provider reconciliation; unknown stays
264	held, matched PRs are reused and merged observations cannot regress through the
265	CLI. These are local consistency checks over caller-attested provider facts.
266	
267	On `dev` or `learn` invocation, `learning.py notices` exposes unread results,
268	including no-change, pending and uncertain states. FO acknowledges a snapshot
269	only after presenting it; a changed digest remains unread. `notices --all` also
270	makes acknowledged jobs available for explicit inspection/recovery. Read-only
271	queries create no learning directory when none exists. Context injection alone
272	is not notification, and a crash before acknowledgement can repeat a notice.
273	
274	A receipt or PR is not an active practice. Subsequent work reads the currently
275	adopted integration version of learning.md, after its separately authorized
276	review/merge path. A recorded merge does not prove a practice improves future
277	work. Harness hooks, automatic polling/background launch, issue reporting and
278	cross-clone deduplication remain future work; the notice step is not an every-host
279	SessionStart guarantee. See the learn skill for the fixed CLI plan/observation
280	schemas, provider checks, recovery and exact delivery authority boundaries.
281	
282	## Maintenance and evidence
283	
284	These are source-repository maintenance commands, not standalone installed-plugin
285	commands. They depend on the repository-level `scripts/skill-frontmatter-lint.sh`
286	and its dependencies. Run from a complete checkout's repository root:
287	
288	```sh
289	python3 kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/lint-skills.py
290	python3 kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/test_sd_dispatch.py --sd-plugin-root /absolute/path/to/active-spacedock
291	```
292	
293	Every other test file is listed in `.github/workflows/kc-dev-flow-2-tests.yml`, which
294	CI runs on each change to this package; run the same commands from there.
295	[`kc-dev-flow-2:maintain-flow`](skills/maintain-flow/SKILL.md) holds the rules for
296	changing the package: the workflow word budget, behaviour replay and observing adopters.
297	
298	Lint reuses `scripts/skill-frontmatter-lint.sh` scoped to this tree and checks
299	declared route coverage, applicability values, exact paths, required principles
300	and skill namespaces, and that every package script named in `skills/` and
301	`references/` is written `<package>/scripts/NAME` and that a skill using `<package>`
302	carries a `Package root:` line. It does not parse rule prose or prove route-following,
303	unknown-profile refusal, gate execution or cross-host parity.
304	The [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) defines
305	frontmatter and directory conventions; complete format validation is a separate
306	authoring check, not a claim made by this CLI.
307	
308	The [adoption reference](references/sd/adoption.md) uses SD commission/refit,
309	split-root state, code worktrees and the activated SD package's unmodified
310	`pr-merge` mod. The mod is installed into the adopting workflow, not vendored here.
311	The workflow's delivery rules preserve project Draft PR, CI and manual merge
312	requirements and restrict unapproved fallback; those are FO instructions, not new
313	mechanical controls. Adoption checks actual `merge: pr-merge` hook discovery before
314	activation: SD can finalize locally when no hook or blocking record exists.
315	
316	The CLI test copies the workflow source into disposable code/state repositories.
317	It checks six stage/host handoffs, stage-definition fetches, PRFAQ/Mermaid gate
318	context, the `## Dispatch facts` section, finding disposition and delivery authority,
319	that scope notes naming the package root reach the dispatch file ahead of the checklist,
320	and that a report ending `- FAILED: none.` is refused by SD and named by its
321	checklist read, and that a correction without a Summary is refused until a complete report follows. Both route graphs across three profiles exercise synthetic gate
322	successors and stamped implementation / validation worktree reuse. Fresh validation is declared configuration, not an
323	executed independent worker. Copied canonical hook discovery and merge-guard
324	arming pass; the missing-hook control demonstrates local finalization's limit.
325	Existing wrong-stage, removed-stage, AC-scanner and host-marker controls remain.
326	`--keep` retains successful repos and raw evidence; failure evidence is retained

# Dev-flow 2

A development workflow run by Spacedock. It provides a thin start/resume entry,
profile principles, stage skills, advisory roles (Chief Engineer, Engineering
Reviewer), a read-only Observer, optional extensions, read-only routing lint, and an adoptable
Spacedock workflow with a POC adaptation. A kc-dev-flow project is not migrated
automatically. Learning runs when invoked by hand or, in a repository that lists the
`learn` extension, by FO when it archives a task; there is no custom runtime loader,
installed hook, background launcher or automatic adoption.

## Controlled trial

Releases are published to this marketplace as `kc-dev-flow-2-vX.Y.Z` tags with
Claude Code and Codex manifests. A reviewed checkout can still be used for a
controlled local trial. For Claude Code, launch
from the intended project with the checkout's absolute package path:

```sh
claude --plugin-dir /absolute/path/to/kc-claude-plugins/kc-dev-flow-2
```

Then invoke `/kc-dev-flow-2:dev`. This is a local package trial, not a published
marketplace release.

For Codex, the marketplace path below is the reviewed **repository root**, not
its `kc-dev-flow-2` subdirectory. Preserve an existing installation; install and
remove only when this trial owns that local plugin change:

```sh
codex -c 'marketplaces.kc-claude-plugins.source_type="local"' \
  -c 'marketplaces.kc-claude-plugins.source="/absolute/path/to/kc-claude-plugins"' \
  plugin add kc-dev-flow-2@kc-claude-plugins

codex -C /absolute/path/to/project \
  -c 'marketplaces.kc-claude-plugins.source_type="local"' \
  -c 'marketplaces.kc-claude-plugins.source="/absolute/path/to/kc-claude-plugins"' \
  -c 'plugins.kc-dev-flow-2@kc-claude-plugins.enabled=true'

# After the trial, remove the plugin installed for this trial.
codex -c 'marketplaces.kc-claude-plugins.source_type="local"' \
  -c 'marketplaces.kc-claude-plugins.source="/absolute/path/to/kc-claude-plugins"' \
  plugin remove kc-dev-flow-2@kc-claude-plugins
```

In the fresh Codex session, request `kc-dev-flow-2:dev` by its exact name. The
commands use per-invocation marketplace overrides; plugin installation itself
persists locally until removed. Bare `/dev`, entry execution and role behavior
remain unproven. Earlier installation/discovery checks found seven skills before
the Engineering Reviewer rename; see [validation scope](VALIDATION.md) for the
historical evidence and its limits.

Spacedock's plugin and CLI are required for orchestration. A project must have an
explicitly selected variant/profile and an approved workflow before
stage work. Follow the [SD adoption reference](references/sd/adoption.md) through
SD commission/refit; invoking the entry does not rewrite a project workflow.

## Entry

Use [`kc-dev-flow-2:dev`](skills/dev/SKILL.md) to start or resume work. It resolves
the explicit project/workflow/task and approved selection, then hands orchestration
to `spacedock:first-officer`. Stage skills keep their own profile routes; the entry
does not migrate existing work or duplicate SD's control loop. Claude plugin skills
use `/kc-dev-flow-2:dev`, not a bare `/dev`; Codex shorthand resolution remains
unverified. Earlier six-skill model reads and later seven-skill discovery do not
prove the new entry executes correctly.

If this package is not yet installed, follow [Controlled trial](#controlled-trial)
for the exact Claude and Codex install commands. If the project has no adopted
Spacedock workflow, follow the [SD adoption reference](references/sd/adoption.md)
directly; the entry only detects and reports that gap, it does not install or
adopt on its own.

## Framework

The First Officer (FO) recommends a profile, records the user's selection and
variant `kc-dev-flow-2` in the work item, aligns the outcome, and orchestrates.
Spacedock (SD) retains stage state, dispatch, reports, gates, feedback and recovery.
A stage skill defines how its selected profile performs work; it does not
advance state, create authority or substitute for an approval.

| Profile | Intended SD route |
| --- | --- |
| [poc](references/profiles/poc.md) | backlog -> implementation -> validation -> done |
| [pilot](references/profiles/pilot.md) | backlog -> ideation -> implementation -> validation -> done |
| [prod](references/profiles/prod.md) | backlog -> ideation -> implementation -> validation -> done |

Backlog is initial and gated; ideation is gated where present; validation is gated
and fresh, with feedback to implementation; done is terminal. Backlog and done
are state boundaries, not worker stages. SD follows ordered stages, so POC uses
a separate four-stage workflow while Pilot/Prod share the five-stage definition.
Only adopt the needed route. Profile remains a user choice on each task and
selects skill rules, not graph transitions. FO holds a profile/graph mismatch;
that check is an instruction, not a new runtime enforcement mechanism.
POC skips ideation and currently uses independent validation. A POC whose proof
creates state or a seam that must outlive the session records `boundary-crossed:`,
and FO returns that choice to the user at the validation gate. Direct POC
eligibility and special Production recovery are **not implemented or proven**.

## Authority and loading

User authority, approved project AGENTS.md conventions and SD contracts constrain
this framework. Within those boundaries, selected profile principles take
precedence over stage practices, which take precedence over conditional project
learning. If an approved requirement conflicts with the selected profile, return
the affected decision to the user; do not silently change profiles or scope.

Each stage SKILL.md owns its sole declared profile routing table. The FO resolves
the recorded variant/profile before dispatch. A dispatched or reused worker
invokes that variant's exact skill and reads the matching shared profile first,
then stage principles, its stage-specific profile reference, and applicable
adopted project learning. A short final profile reminder is enough; do not load
all profiles or repeat the entire shared rules. Unknown selections, missing
inputs/references or unresolved authority conflicts require a hold report.
These are skill instructions, not mechanically unskippable runtime gates.

Engineering Reviewer provides independent technical assurance; CE (Chief Engineer)
advises the next smallest integrated delivery step. Their agents and skills retain
the existing role boundaries and Opus/xhigh policy. Neither is a routine gate,
and POC defaults to no consultation. Observer reads FO's writes to one task's
state against the workflow rules; its agent declares Sonnet, and it reports without
repairing. The design director reviews a ui task's pictures and screenshots and
rules on each decline the author or validator proposes; its agent declares Sonnet, and
it advises and holds no gate. Exact `kc-dev-flow-2:` references prevent
declared links from accidentally selecting the baseline; actual host resolution
still needs a separate behavioral test.

## Design and delivery

FO leads direction and requests research only when it can change a decision;
workers author the bounded deliverable. For a route that includes ideation,
use a PRFAQ with Mermaid whose actors, order, branches and approval boundaries
match the prose. FO's recorded `Surfaces:` line picks the owed artifact: a `ui`
preview, a `db` schema, or `none` for PRFAQ/Mermaid alone;
`scripts/design_surfaces.py check --seed` checks seed fields and the FO record before a new task is
admitted; its default mode checks the markers, the artifacts, a usable
`## Acceptance criteria` section and any `## Captain amendments` before the gate.
A change the Captain makes after accepting a design is recorded there and applied
by the next worker, as [workflow](references/sd/workflow.md) states.
A task that belongs to a release on a journey map triggers one whole-journey review
of that release before its tasks are split; [workflow](references/sd/workflow.md)
gives the signals and the single checkpoint.
Write material corrections back to the same definition before user approval.
Implementation follows approved scope; validation checks the exact result and
returns repairs through the supported feedback route. POC must not gain
an ideation stage or extra design gate through this convention; its boundary
crossing is a report marker, not a design gate.

When work changes retained documents or behavior they describe, stage skills load
one [document reference](references/retained-documents.md) for affected claims,
unique content and rendered diagram agreement. Validation also checks whether
its decisive checks can catch relevant errors, reusing existing counterexamples.
These conditional practices add no mandatory architecture file or global audit.

FO also owns landing a ruling that outlives the task, written by the implementation
worker and checked at validation — see [workflow](references/sd/workflow.md)'s
Decision records. A capability a user will get, named in conversation and
deferred, belongs on the product's journey map instead.

The [workflow source](references/sd/workflow.md) defines limited FO design
corrections and nonblocking dispositions. Template adoption grants no editing
permission; approved decisions and worker evidence remain protected.

Continuous stage-pin sealing and its kernel loader are intentionally omitted.
Git history and SD records do not prove which content was used at a historical
stage entry. This package does not fix the baseline's skipped-pin bug or
claim equivalent tamper detection.

## Extensions

Optional tools join as extensions in [`extensions/`](extensions/), each described by its
`EXTENSION.md`. An adopter lists the ones it uses under `extensions:` in its workflow
README frontmatter; an unlisted extension is not probed and changes nothing. The
workflow's `## Extensions` section is the rule FO follows. The template lists the `required`
rows; the install ask in [`adoption.md`](references/sd/adoption.md) offers the rest, and
`scripts/lint-skills.py` checks that the `required` rows and the template line agree.

| Extension | Tier | Joins | Adds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [codex](extensions/codex/EXTENSION.md) | recommended | FO review rounds and the merge ask | reads Codex GitHub review rounds on the PR head |
| [roborev](extensions/roborev/EXTENSION.md) | recommended | implementation, before the report | a local roborev review of the committed changes |
| [peers](extensions/peers/EXTENSION.md) | required | FO, before opening a task or exchanging peer facts | selects the peer transport, permits confirmed Paseo asks and replies without paseo listing, searches existing work and checks facts within existing authority |
| [paseo](extensions/paseo/EXTENSION.md) | optional, requires peers | FO, before a listed Paseo Codex worker dispatch | selects its worker publication and local-review handoff; peers owns peer asks and replies |
| [copilot](extensions/copilot/EXTENSION.md) | optional | FO review rounds, each push and the merge ask | requests and reads GitHub Copilot review rounds on the PR head |
| [learn](extensions/learn/EXTENSION.md) | required | FO, through the `kc-dev-flow-2` mod in `references/sd/mods/`, before the merge sentinel and right after a task is archived | checks `observer.md` is committed before the sentinel (`scripts/observer_check.py`), runs `learn` and the observer, and presents both results |
| [journey-map](extensions/journey-map/EXTENSION.md) | recommended | FO, after a gate ruling on a journey task, before `merge guard`, and after the archive | writes a footprint for a ruling that answers a map question, checks it before the merge guard, and folds it into the map as a docs-only pull request |
| [release-acceptance](extensions/release-acceptance/EXTENSION.md) | recommended, with journey-map | an acceptance task for a release, from implementation to the validation gate and the close | walks a finished release with reviewers on different Claude models, has the design director rule on their complaints and the deferred findings, and records the walk in the task folder |
| [fo-feedback](extensions/fo-feedback/EXTENSION.md) | optional, requires peers | interviewing maintainer, at attended resume and named batch close | gathers operator experience every three completed batches beside independent observer findings |

## Learning loop

Optional [operator feedback](extensions/fo-feedback/EXTENSION.md) records failures,
workarounds and useful events; findings follow the existing backlog and Captain decisions.

The loop runs on three lines. Project learning: `learn` evaluates one closed task and
may propose a root learning.md rule as a Draft PR. Package improvement: the
[observer](skills/observer/SKILL.md) reads what FO wrote into one task's state
against the workflow rules, at archive and when a maintainer reads an adopter's first
task after a release, and a rule broken in two tasks becomes a package change under
`maintain-flow`. Deciding for the Captain: `scripts/decision_ledger.py` derives every
gate ruling from the task files SD already writes, and FO decides only within the
delegation ladder of [ADR 0011](https://github.com/iamcxa/kc-claude-plugins/blob/main/docs/adr/0011-fo-decides-for-the-captain-by-a-delegation-ladder.md);
[ADR 0009](https://github.com/iamcxa/kc-claude-plugins/blob/main/docs/adr/0009-self-improvement-is-a-three-position-switch-unlocked-by-change-class.md)
keeps package self-improvement manual.

Use [`kc-dev-flow-2:learn`](skills/learn/SKILL.md) for one explicitly named closed
task. FO verifies committed SD archive state and the original repository-qualified
merged GitHub PR through existing read interfaces, then delegates independent
evaluation. Missing or contradictory evidence holds learning without reopening
the development task. This is skill-led verification; the Python helper still
records supplied facts and does not authenticate SD or GitHub.

Use [`kc-dev-flow-2:evaluate-learning`](skills/evaluate-learning/SKILL.md) for a
bounded independent assessment of explicitly supplied task evidence. Its three
outcomes are add, no-change and remove; a rewrite combines remove/add. Entries
contain Applicability, Practice and Evidence. One task supports one case; reading
a rule or green tests alone does not prove improvement. No applicable case is
not grounds for deletion, and unknown attribution stays unknown. Fixed project
rules require separate user-approved adoption into AGENTS.md; no auto-promotion,
scores or maturity system is introduced.

The skill documents the strict evidence-pack and evaluation JSON formats and
commands for `scripts/learning.py`. This stdlib helper records eligibility from
caller-supplied closure/merge facts; it does **not** verify SD or GitHub truth.
It stores one atomic record under the Git common directory's
`kc-dev-flow-2/learning/`, shared by linked worktrees in the same clone. An opaque
claim token binds completion to its pending attempt. Invalid results leave that
claim repairable; duplicate triggers observe it rather than launch another job.
A store-wide lock also serializes new claims against each other: while one job's
directory has a torn or missing record, its evaluation is pending, or its
completed proposal has no settled delivery (merged, closed, or explicitly
released), a `claim` for any other job in the same store is refused, naming the
blocking job. Re-claiming the same job is unaffected. A proposal the Captain
declines to deliver needs an explicit `release`; no CLI command removes or
rewrites `release.json`, so a release cannot be undone. A closed delivery
cannot be released; a released job whose delivery was missing or confirmed
absent can still later be observed `open` (a PR turns up that the release
believed did not exist) — that observation blocks again, because a release
stops a job from blocking, it does not stop the provider from reporting new
facts about it.
A completed record contains both evaluation and local proposal; no-change has no
proposal. No recorder command writes learning.md, AGENTS.md or workflow state.

Pending ownership is not process liveness. Torn/missing records are uncertain;
recovery requires a current record digest and an explicit caller attestation
that the prior owner stopped. It preserves prior bytes and revokes the old token.
Completed results cannot be replaced through this CLI. POSIX file locking and
atomic replacement cover cooperating callers on local filesystems, not separate
clones, distributed locks or protection from a process with the same file access.

A changed result can be materialized by an author in an owned isolated worktree,
changing only root learning.md. The evaluated integration commit/learning blob
must still match before publication. User commit and delivery authority remain
required; a no-change result creates no branch or PR. A job-derived branch/body
marker supports all-state PR lookup. Reuse a fully matching existing PR; conflicting
or unknown provider evidence holds rather than sending another one.

The recorder keeps delivery ownership/observations in a separate atomic sidecar,
leaving completed evaluation bytes immutable. It binds the reviewed result, repo,
branch, candidate and learning blobs, plus exact PR title/body. Claiming records
uncertainty before remote effects; existing claims grant no automatic resend.
FO uses existing Git/gh commands to publish a Draft PR and record observed state.
A failed response does not prove the send failed. Explicit stopped-owner recovery
requires a current digest and successful provider reconciliation; unknown stays
held, matched PRs are reused and merged observations cannot regress through the
CLI. These are local consistency checks over caller-attested provider facts.

On `dev` or `learn` invocation, `learning.py notices` exposes unread results,
including no-change, pending and uncertain states. FO acknowledges a snapshot
only after presenting it; a changed digest remains unread. `notices --all` also
makes acknowledged jobs available for explicit inspection/recovery. Read-only
queries create no learning directory when none exists. Context injection alone
is not notification, and a crash before acknowledgement can repeat a notice.

A receipt or PR is not an active practice. Subsequent work reads the currently
adopted integration version of learning.md, after its separately authorized
review/merge path. A recorded merge does not prove a practice improves future
work. Harness hooks, automatic polling/background launch, issue reporting and
cross-clone deduplication remain future work; the notice step is not an every-host
SessionStart guarantee. See the learn skill for the fixed CLI plan/observation
schemas, provider checks, recovery and exact delivery authority boundaries.

## Maintenance and evidence

These are source-repository maintenance commands, not standalone installed-plugin
commands. They depend on the repository-level `scripts/skill-frontmatter-lint.sh`
and its dependencies. Run from a complete checkout's repository root:

```sh
python3 kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/lint-skills.py
python3 kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/test_sd_dispatch.py --sd-plugin-root /absolute/path/to/active-spacedock
```

Every other test file is listed in `.github/workflows/kc-dev-flow-2-tests.yml`, which
CI runs on each change to this package; run the same commands from there.
[`kc-dev-flow-2:maintain-flow`](skills/maintain-flow/SKILL.md) holds the rules for
changing the package: the workflow word budget, behaviour replay and observing adopters.

Lint reuses `scripts/skill-frontmatter-lint.sh` scoped to this tree and checks
declared route coverage, applicability values, exact paths, required principles
and skill namespaces, and that every package script named in `skills/` and
`references/` is written `<package>/scripts/NAME` and that a skill using `<package>`
carries a `Package root:` line. It does not parse rule prose or prove route-following,
unknown-profile refusal, gate execution or cross-host parity.
The [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) defines
frontmatter and directory conventions; complete format validation is a separate
authoring check, not a claim made by this CLI.

The [adoption reference](references/sd/adoption.md) uses SD commission/refit,
split-root state, code worktrees and the activated SD package's unmodified
`pr-merge` mod. The mod is installed into the adopting workflow, not vendored here.
The workflow's delivery rules preserve project Draft PR, CI and manual merge
requirements and restrict unapproved fallback; those are FO instructions, not new
mechanical controls. Adoption checks actual `merge: pr-merge` hook discovery before
activation: SD can finalize locally when no hook or blocking record exists.

The CLI test copies the workflow source into disposable code/state repositories.
It checks six stage/host handoffs, stage-definition fetches, PRFAQ/Mermaid gate
context, the `## Dispatch facts` section, finding disposition and delivery authority,
that scope notes naming the package root reach the dispatch file ahead of the checklist,
and that a report ending `- FAILED: none.` is refused by SD and named by its
checklist read, and that a correction without a Summary is refused until a complete report follows. Both route graphs across three profiles exercise synthetic gate
successors and stamped implementation / validation worktree reuse. Fresh validation is declared configuration, not an
executed independent worker. Copied canonical hook discovery and merge-guard
arming pass; the missing-hook control demonstrates local finalization's limit.
Existing wrong-stage, removed-stage, AC-scanner and host-marker controls remain.
`--keep` retains successful repos and raw evidence; failure evidence is retained
by default. Synthetic approvals and local archive controls are test inputs,
not real user acceptance, hook execution or remote delivery. No prompt is sent
to a model. A real project still needs approved configuration and observed merge.

For an authorized native Claude trial, remove foreign markers for that process
only: `env -u CODEX_THREAD_ID -u PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR claude <approved arguments>`.
Use the exact isolated repository as cwd, name its workflow explicitly in the FO
assignment, and retain `--workflow-dir` on SD commands. Do not change the parent
environment or add a wrapper. The model-free marker check is not a rerun of the
native trial, and a failed stamped dispatch must not be assumed mutation-free.
Before a future live run, verify the selected SD plugin and executable versions;
an updated skill cache alone does not establish a comparable runtime.
At ideation, retain user gate approval while proposing routine implementation
details within accepted scope; escalate material changes rather than every detail.

Future comparisons must include host behavior, retained route exceptions and
learning/review costs as well as removed files. This slice runs no model
experiment and carries forward none of the earlier experiment's time budget.

293	Before repair authorization, product bytes and the recorded candidate revision stay

306	  boundary or value acceptance criterion.

308	  record what would make it material.
